text:
nina: Heads up — after the exports cleanup I noticed the SDK typings disappear for subpath imports in a couple of our sample apps (vite + pnpm). Example: `import { createClient } from '@redwood-inference/sdk/chat'` fails to find declarations.
omar: that sounds like missing types in the exports subpath. Do we have per-subpath `types` entries?
nina: nope, package.json currently has only a top-level "types": "dist/esm/index.d.ts" and exports subpaths only specify import/require.
kate: modern TS and some bundlers consult exports subpaths for types. If the subpath lacks a types entry resolution fails.
ci-bot: quick suggestion: add "types": "./dist/types/chat/index.d.ts" to the `./chat` exports entry and publish types in the package.
omar: also observed resolver differences: bun/deno resolve exports conditions differently; they sometimes pick CJS path which has no named exports and then runtime errors surface as `The requested module ... does not provide an export named 'createClient'`.
nina: repro: vite dev server uses Edge target and ends up pulling `require` entry. HMR flakes with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'`.
kate: short-term workaround for samples: add a `module` field pointing to ESM build or update example imports to `@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/chat`. Not ideal though.
omar: longer-term: update sdk exports ordering to prefer `edge`/`browser`/`import` before `require`, and add explicit `types` per subpath and a `dist/types` build step.
ci-bot: action items:
- add `edge` & `browser` export conditions before `require` (omar)
- expose `types` under each public subpath and include `dist/types` in package (kate)
- add a tiny CI job that installs the packed tarball and runs `tsc --noEmit` against sample imports (nina)
- document bundler quirks in SDK migration note (omar)
kate: I'll open the PR with the types generation and update package.json exports. nina: will add the tsc check to examples CI. ci-bot: Attach PRs to DEVEX-430.
nina: tip — when debugging local resolution run `node --trace-resolve` or use `resolve.exports` to see which condition matched.
omar: thanks, will follow up after PR lands 👍
